newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes higher on seasonal recovery.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes higher on seasonal recovery.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on commercial and fund buying tied to a seasonal recovery, traders said.
"Seasonally, wheat should be moving higher," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
The U.S. winter wheat harvest was beginning to wind down and wheat futures recently had fallen to contract lows amid the combining of an excellent crop.
Cargill Inc bought three million bushels of September and two million December, traders said. Rosenthal Collins and Prudential Securities were said to be key late buyers.
The commercial demand led to talk that an export sale of U.S. wheat may have been made, the traders said.

Also there was talk Egypt had delayed for three months a ban on importation of genetically-altered grains. But there is no genetically altered wheat on the market and U.S. exports of wheat and animal feed to Egypt should not be affected.
Wheat was pressured in early dealings on a drop in corn and soybean futures.
Wheat closed two to 4-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with July up four at $3.32-1/2. September was up 4-1/4 at $3.40-1/4.
In spread trading, LFG Futures did 500,000 March/December at 10-1/4 cents, premium March and LIT America did 200,000 December/July at 22 cents, premium December, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 21,000 contracts, above the 14,360 traded Friday.
In wheat options, E.D. and F. Man Interntional sold 800 September $3.50 calls at three to 3-1/2 cents and bought 300 December $3.70 calls at 10-3/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 7,000 contracts, above the 4,984 traded Friday.
